name: John and Bartha Moulton Homestead
summary: A three-part northern Mormon Row cluster: the gambrel-with-shed log barn is the hero, the pink stucco house is a companion landmark, and the surviving minor buildings are a shared-material context batch.

structures.name: John and Bartha Moulton Residence (Pink House)

placement.reason: The current buildings extract contains plausible unnamed footprints but no stable John Moulton names.
placement.strategy: Match the northern Mormon Row unnamed building footprints to the HABS site geometry and measured plans; do not place from a single photograph or from the nearby T. A. Moulton landmark.

constraints.subject: pink_house
constraints.relationship: approximately 70 feet west of Mormon Row Road and 300 feet north of Antelope Flats Road

constraints.subject: barn
constraints.relationship: approximately 135 feet northeast of the house

resolution_steps: Extract plan dimensions and north arrows from HABS WY-152-A and WY-152-C.
Derive the Mormon Row Road and Antelope Flats Road intersection and road bearings from the current geospatial source.
Score unnamed footprints by HABS offset residual, plan dimensions, orientation, topology, and agreement with current orthophotography.
Accept only a unique primary-structure match; otherwise georeference the HABS site plan to orthophotography and digitize explicit replacement footprints.
Persist source feature IDs, source hashes, centers, rotations, footprints, residuals, and confidence in the draft placement artifact.

budgets.material_policy: Share compact timber, roof, stucco, and trim material families across the cluster; a registered projection may be added only to close-facing hero surfaces.

lods.intent: Recognizable openings, gambrel transitions, house trim, and restrained ground-contact detail.
Retain the barn's gambrel-with-shed silhouette, the house's 1.5-story profile, and primary openings.
Silhouette and broad barn/house material split only.

required_views.purpose: Primary public-facing elevation and opening layout.
Gambrel-to-shed transition, log character, and corner continuity.
Pink stucco field, green trim, and measured opening arrangement.

prompt_constraints: Preserve the exact registered target silhouette, roof topology, framing, crop, camera, and transparent/background mask.
Use only references identified as the same John Moulton structure; never use T. A. Moulton Barn imagery.
The barn must remain a two-story gambrel-with-shed log barn; do not convert it to a simple gable or T. A.'s gable-with-sheds form.
The house must remain a 1.5-story frame house with restrained salmon/pink stucco and historically supported green door/window trim.
Do not infer dimensions, roof pitch, placement, openings, or additions from image generation.
Do not add landscape, mountains, people, animals, vehicles, text, watermarks, extra windows, new doors, featureless black rectangles, or baked cast shadows.
Keep tileable materials free of perspective, vegetation, sky, and directional sunlight.

checks: projection registration at frontal and grazing angles
no production asset or manifest mutation

conditions: Barn or house lacks an official HABS/NPS identity source.
Barn or house lacks one measured drawing and at least two useful exterior elevations.
Any acquired artifact lacks URL, author/creator, rights statement, retrieval date, and SHA-256.
A visual reference cannot be proven to show the John Moulton structure rather than T. A. Moulton Barn.
Primary footprint match is not unique at confidence 0.85 or higher.
Primary center uncertainty exceeds 3 metres or orientation uncertainty exceeds 5 degrees.
Barn-to-house arrangement conflicts with the HABS site geometry.
Barn gambrel-with-shed topology or house 1.5-story profile is not recognizable in every LOD.
Generated dimensions are not traceable to HABS drawings, LiDAR, or an explicitly marked estimate.
Roofs intersect walls incorrectly, daylight gaps appear at roof junctions, or foundations float.
Projection edges drift from the approved orthographic target.
Black placeholder openings, cross-building reference contamination, baked landscape, or invented architectural features are visible.
Vegetation clearing removes documented trees, corrals, fences, or irrigation context beyond physical clearance.
Any cluster triangle, draw-call, texture-transfer, or LOD activation budget is exceeded.
The combined Mormon Row capture regresses the agreed High-quality performance baseline.
